lines.en: Lesson 54
lines.zh: 第54课

lines.en: Instinct or cleverness?
lines.zh: 本能还是智慧？

lines.en: Was the writer successful in protecting his peach tree? Why not?
lines.zh: 作者成功保护了他的桃树吗？为什么没有？

lines.en: We have been brought up to fear insects.
lines.zh: 我们从小就被教导要害怕昆虫。

lines.en: We regard them as unnecessary creatures that do more harm than good.
lines.zh: 我们认为它们是多余的生物，弊大于利。

lines.en: We continually wage war on them, for they contaminate our food, carry diseases, or devour our crops.
lines.zh: 我们不断地与它们作斗争，因为它们会污染我们的食物，传播疾病，或吞噬我们的庄稼。

lines.en: They sting or bite without provocation; they fly uninvited into our rooms on summer nights, or beat against our lighted windows.
lines.zh: 它们无故蜇人或咬人；在夏天的夜晚，它们不请自来地飞进我们的房间，或拍打我们点亮的窗户。

lines.en: We live in dread not only of unpleasant insects like spiders or wasps, but of quite harmless ones like moths.
lines.zh: 我们不仅害怕蜘蛛或黄蜂等令人不快的昆虫，也害怕像飞蛾这样完全无害的昆虫。

lines.en: Reading about them increases our understanding without dispelling our fears.
lines.zh: 阅读有关它们的文章增加了我们的理解，却无法消除我们的恐惧。

lines.en: Knowing that the industrious ant lives in a highly organized society
lines.zh: 即使知道勤劳的蚂蚁生活在一个高度组织化的社会中，

lines.en: does nothing to prevent us from being filled with revulsion when we find hordes of them crawling over a carefully prepared picnic lunch.
lines.zh: 也无法阻止我们在一群蚂蚁爬满精心准备的野餐时感到厌恶。

lines.en: No matter how much we like honey,
lines.zh: 无论我们多么喜欢蜂蜜，

lines.en: or how much we have read about the uncanny sense of direction which bees possess, we have a horror of being stung.
lines.zh: 无论我们读过多少关于蜜蜂拥有不可思议的方向感，我们都害怕被蜇。

lines.en: Most of our fears are unreasonable, but they are impossible to erase.
lines.zh: 我们大部分的恐惧都是不合理的，但它们又难以消除。

lines.en: At the same time, however, insects are strangely fascinating.
lines.zh: 然而，与此同时，昆虫又有着奇特的魅力。

lines.en: We enjoy reading about them, especially when we find that, like the praying mantis, they lead perfectly horrible lives.
lines.zh: 我们喜欢阅读有关它们的文章，特别是当我们发现，像螳螂一样，它们过着极其可怕的生活时。

lines.en: We enjoy staring at them, entranced as they go about their business, unaware (we hope) of our presence.
lines.zh: 我们喜欢凝视它们，着迷地看着它们忙碌，希望它们没有察觉到我们的存在。

lines.en: Who has not stood in awe at the sight of a spider pouncing on a fly,
lines.zh: 谁不曾敬畏地看着蜘蛛扑向苍蝇，

lines.en: or a column of ants triumphantly bearing home an enormous dead beetle?
lines.zh: 或一队蚂蚁凯旋地将一只巨大的死甲虫搬回家呢？

lines.en: Last summer I spent days in the garden watching thousands of ants crawling up the trunk of my prize peach tree.
lines.zh: 去年夏天，我在花园里花了好几天时间，观察成千上万的蚂蚁爬上我那棵珍贵的桃树树干。

lines.en: The tree has grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house.
lines.zh: 这棵树长在房子避风处的一面暖墙边。

lines.en: I am especially proud of it,
lines.zh: 我特别为它感到自豪，

lines.en: not only because it has survived several severe winters, but because it occasionally produces luscious peaches.
lines.zh: 不仅因为它熬过了好几个严酷的冬天，还因为它偶尔会结出甜美的桃子。

lines.en: During the summer, I noticed that the leaves of the tree were beginning to wither.
lines.zh: 夏天的时候，我注意到树叶开始枯萎了。

lines.en: Clusters of tiny insects called aphides were to be found on the underside of the leaves.
lines.zh: 树叶的背面可以发现成群的微小昆虫，叫做蚜虫。

lines.en: They were visited by a large colony of ants which obtained a sort of honey from them.
lines.zh: 一大群蚂蚁来访，从它们那里获取一种蜜露。

lines.en: I immediately embarked on an experiment which even though it failed to get rid of the ants kept me fascinated for twenty-four hours.
lines.zh: 我立即开始了一项实验，尽管它未能除掉蚂蚁，但却让我着迷了二十四个小时。

lines.en: I bound the base of the tree with sticky tape, making it impossible for the ants to reach the aphides.
lines.zh: 我用胶带缠住了树的底部，使蚂蚁无法接触到蚜虫。

lines.en: The tape was so sticky that they did not dare to cross it.
lines.zh: 胶带非常粘，它们不敢越过。

lines.en: For a long time, I watched them scurrying around the base of the tree in bewilderment.
lines.zh: 我长时间地看着它们困惑地在树底跑来跑去。

lines.en: I even went out at midnight with a torch and noted with satisfaction (and surprise)
lines.zh: 我甚至在午夜带着手电筒出去，满意地（也惊讶地）注意到

lines.en: that the ants were still swarming around the sticky tape without being able to do anything about it.
lines.zh: 蚂蚁仍然在胶带周围聚集，却无计可施。

lines.en: I got up early next morning hoping to find that the ants had given up in despair.
lines.zh: 第二天早上我早早起床，希望能看到蚂蚁已经绝望地放弃了。

lines.en: Instead, I saw that they had discovered a new route.
lines.zh: 结果，我发现它们开辟了一条新路线。

lines.en: They were climbing up the wall of the house and then on to the leaves of the tree.
lines.zh: 它们正在爬上房子的墙壁，然后爬到树叶上。

lines.en: I realized sadly that I had been completely defeated by their ingenuity.
lines.zh: 我伤心地意识到，我完全被它们的足智多谋打败了。

lines.en: The ants had been quick to find an answer to my thoroughly unscientific methods!
lines.zh: 蚂蚁很快就找到了应对我这种完全不科学的方法的办法！
